name: Patagonia Glacier + Torres Family Adventure

dates.why: Built to match the current comparison window: depart Monday, August 31 and return Sunday, September 13.

exchangeRateNote: International lodging/activity costs are USD planning estimates; live booking should re-price in local currency before purchase.
positioning: A higher-effort, higher-cost adventure option built around Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Perito Moreno Glacier, El Chalten, Puerto Natales, and Torres del Paine, scaled down for two adults and a one-year-old.
routeRationale: Use Buenos Aires as the necessary buffer before and after Patagonia flights.
Start Argentine Patagonia at El Calafate because Perito Moreno has the best infrastructure for a baby.
Add El Chalten for Fitz Roy scenery but keep hikes short and optional.
Use Puerto Natales as the practical Torres del Paine base instead of pricey in-park lodges.
Return to Buenos Aires the day before the ATL flight to avoid same-day Patagonia-to-USA risk.

recommended.label: Delta-first Buenos Aires + domestic Patagonia legs
recommended.infantNote: Budget includes two adult ATL-EZE round trips, domestic Patagonia legs, and infant-in-lap estimate. Re-price exact AR/LATAM domestic times before booking.

bases.name: Buenos Aires buffer
bases.why: Protects the domestic Patagonia connection after the overnight flight.

bases.name: El Calafate glacier base
bases.why: Best base for Perito Moreno with services, food, and weather backups.

bases.name: El Chalten mountain village base
bases.why: Fitz Roy scenery with short trails from town.

bases.name: Puerto Natales / Torres base
bases.hotel: Weskar Lodge / Puerto Natales family room
bases.why: More practical and cheaper than in-park lodges while still reaching Torres del Paine.

dailyItinerary.title: Delta overnight ATL to Buenos Aires
dailyItinerary.transport: Depart ATL on Delta ATL-EZE planning snapshot, overnight to Buenos Aires; book two adult tickets and add infant-in-lap.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Long-haul logistics day: choose the simplest Delta-first Buenos Aires routing before adding Patagonia domestic legs.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If Delta nonstop pricing is poor, compare Delta/LATAM partner-style routings while preserving a Buenos Aires overnight buffer.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport dinner and baby flight snacks; budget $100.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Infant-in-lap, bassinet/bulkhead request, and a conservative connection plan for domestic Patagonia flights.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book international flights first, then domestic flights to El Calafate.
dailyItinerary.why: Patagonia is worth considering, but only if the logistics are honest: this day anchors the long international hop and preserves a buffer before flying south.
moments: Choose the least complicated ATL-EZE routing.
Add the infant directly with Delta.
Do not connect straight through to Patagonia after the overnight flight.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport includes international + Patagonia domestic flight budget for two adults plus infant estimate.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Buenos Aires recovery day
dailyItinerary.transport: Airport transfer to Recoleta/Palermo hotel; no car.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Sleep reset, stroller walk in Recoleta parks, grocery/snack setup, and early dinner.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If arrival is smooth, add a short Palermo botanical garden stroll.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Cafe lunch, grocery run, early parrilla/Italian dinner; budget $210.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: This day exists for sleep, food, and body-clock adjustment before Patagonia.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book hotel with crib, elevator, and easy taxi access.
dailyItinerary.why: A Buenos Aires buffer dramatically lowers risk: no same-day domestic flight scramble, no missed bags drama, and a kinder start for a one-year-old.
moments: Hotel check-in and nap matter more than sightseeing.
Use parks/cafes for gentle city texture.
Prep snacks/diapers for the flight south.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Local transfer and city food only.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Fly to El Calafate and settle by Lago Argentino
dailyItinerary.transport: Fly Buenos Aires to El Calafate on Aerolineas Argentinas/LATAM planning snapshot; taxi to hotel.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Domestic flight south, check into El Calafate, lakefront walk, and early dinner.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If flight times shift late, make this a pure arrival/hotel day.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport snacks, El Calafate dinner; budget $195.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Keep the Patagonia arrival low-pressure; request crib and kettle.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book domestic flight with enough checked-bag/car-seat padding.
dailyItinerary.why: El Calafate is the practical glacier gateway and the easiest Patagonia landing spot before deeper park travel.
moments: Let Lago Argentino be the first Patagonia view.
Do not add a glacier excursion after flying.
Use town services for supplies before the park days.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Domestic flight budget is allocated in Day 1; this covers local arrival transfer.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Perito Moreno Glacier boardwalks
dailyItinerary.transport: Private transfer or rental car to Perito Moreno Glacier, about 80 minutes each way.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Perito Moreno Glacier boardwalk circuit with flexible viewpoints, lunch, and no boat unless the baby is thriving.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If weather is terrible, do Glaciarium museum and lakeside cafes, then move the glacier to Day 5.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Packed lunch/cafe, El Calafate dinner; budget $210.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier preferred for boardwalks; stroller may work in limited areas but not as the only plan.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm park entry, transfer pickup, and weather before booking extras.
dailyItinerary.why: This is Patagonia’s highest-confidence “wow” day: world-class glacier scenery with boardwalk infrastructure that can work for a family.
moments: Arrive early and choose the easiest boardwalk sections.
Listen for glacier calving from safe viewpoints.
Skip add-ons if the baby needs a shorter day.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activities cover park entry and transfer/tour buffer for two adults.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Estancia or Glaciarium flexible day
dailyItinerary.transport: Short local transfer or estancia pickup depending on chosen plan.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Choose a gentle estancia-style day near El Calafate for animals/open space, or Glaciarium museum plus lakefront recovery if weather is poor.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Pure town day: playground, cafes, laundry, and nap recovery before El Chalten.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Estancia lunch if booked or town lunch/dinner; budget $220.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: This is the baby-friendly counterweight to the glacier day: animals/space or indoor museum.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Pick estancia only if transfer times are reasonable with naps.
dailyItinerary.why: Patagonia can become a string of long drives; this day keeps El Calafate useful and family-scaled.
moments: Let animals/open space be the activity if the estancia timing works.
Keep Glaciarium as a strong weather backup.
Use the afternoon for laundry and packing.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Estancia option may push this day higher; Glaciarium version is cheaper.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Transfer to El Chalten mountain village
dailyItinerary.transport: El Calafate to El Chalten by rental car or private transfer, about 3 hours plus stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Scenic transfer along Ruta 40/23, arrival in El Chalten, and short village/river walk under Fitz Roy if clear.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If wind/weather is rough, make this a straight transfer and hotel dinner.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Road lunch/snacks, El Chalten dinner; budget $205.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Nap-drive day; keep arrival walk optional.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Reserve transfer/rental car and lodging early; El Chalten inventory is limited.
dailyItinerary.why: El Chalten is the mountain-hike heart of Argentine Patagonia, but the plan keeps hikes short and carrier-friendly.
moments: Use the drive as the nap.
Stop for the first Fitz Roy view if weather opens.
Settle into town before attempting trails.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transfer cost assumes private/rental logistics, not the cheapest bus-only option.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Mirador Los Condores and Fitz Roy views
dailyItinerary.transport: Walk from town trailheads or short taxi positioning.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Mirador Los Condores / Las Aguilas short carrier hike for Fitz Roy valley views, then town lunch and nap.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If wind is too strong, do visitor center, cafes, and a low river walk.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier hike only; choose turnaround based on wind and baby tolerance.
dailyItinerary.why: This gives the Chalten mountain payoff without committing to Laguna de los Tres mileage.
moments: Start early for calmer wind.
Keep the hike short and celebratory.
Spend the afternoon in town instead of stacking trails.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Laguna Capri light version or Rio de las Vueltas
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Attempt a conservative Laguna Capri partial hike if conditions are excellent; otherwise Rio de las Vueltas viewpoints and town recovery.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Do Chorrillo del Salto waterfall instead for a shorter, easier outing.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Packed lunch or town cafe, early dinner; budget $205.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: This is the most hike-like day; carrier, layers, and a strict turnaround are required.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Do not force this day in bad wind/weather.
dailyItinerary.why: It preserves the possibility of a classic Fitz Roy hiking moment while being honest about traveling with a one-year-old.
moments: Set a turnaround time before starting.
Choose Chorrillo del Salto if the baby or wind says no.
Keep dinner easy after trail time.
dailyItinerary.costNote: No paid activity; budget sits in food/logistics.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Long transfer to Puerto Natales
dailyItinerary.overnight: Weskar Lodge / Puerto Natales family room
dailyItinerary.transport: El Chalten to Puerto Natales by private transfer/rental combo, staged border day, about 6-7 hours before stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Big logistics day across the border into Chilean Patagonia; check into Puerto Natales and walk the waterfront if energy allows.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the border/drive feels too much, break the route with an extra El Calafate night and shorten Chile.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Road snacks, simple Puerto Natales dinner; budget $215.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: This is the hardest baby logistics day. Build stops, snacks, and no evening plans.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm border requirements, transfer provider, and car-seat availability.
dailyItinerary.why: Puerto Natales unlocks Torres del Paine without forcing everyone to sleep inside the park at peak prices.
moments: Treat the transfer as the only objective.
Use the waterfront as a gentle arrival reset.
Keep backup lodging flexibility if border timing changes.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport is high because this cross-border leg likely needs private transfer/rental logistics.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Torres del Paine first viewpoints
dailyItinerary.overnight: Weskar Lodge / Puerto Natales family room
dailyItinerary.transport: Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine viewpoints and back, long day with flexible stops.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Torres del Paine scenic drive: Lago Sarmiento/Laguna Amarga approach, Salto Grande area if conditions allow, and viewpoint picnic.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If wind/weather is too much, do Milodon Cave and Puerto Natales waterfront instead.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Mostly car/viewpoint day; carrier for short paths, avoid exposed wind if severe.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Buy/confirm park entry and check road/weather reports.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the Chilean Patagonia money view day, designed as viewpoints and short walks rather than a famous trek.
moments: Enter the park with no major hike agenda.
Use Salto Grande only if wind is manageable.
Let the baby reset in the car between viewpoints.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Includes park entry and fuel/transfer buffer.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Lago Grey or estancia-style Patagonia day
dailyItinerary.overnight: Weskar Lodge / Puerto Natales family room
dailyItinerary.transport: Puerto Natales to Lago Grey/park sector or local estancia alternative.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Choose Lago Grey beach/viewpoint day if weather is clear, or a lower-key estancia/wildlife-style outing closer to Puerto Natales.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Use Puerto Natales town, cafes, playground, and hotel views as the recovery option.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Picnic or estancia lunch, Puerto Natales dinner; budget $225.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Keep boat/glacier extras optional; wind can make baby comfort the deciding factor.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book any Lago Grey boat/estancia only after weather check.
dailyItinerary.why: This adds a second Torres del Paine texture without making the trip depend on one perfect park day.
moments: Decide morning-of based on wind.
Choose views and animals over mileage.
Keep afternoon recovery sacred.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity budget covers either park/boat-adjacent costs or estancia-style outing.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Puerto Natales slow day and final Patagonia views
dailyItinerary.overnight: Weskar Lodge / Puerto Natales family room
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Waterfront walk, town cafes, gear/laundry reset, optional Milodon Cave if skipped earlier, and final mountain-view dinner.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Pure hotel/lounge day if weather is ugly or everyone is tired.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Cafe lunch, nicer final Patagonia dinner; budget $240.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: This is intentionally a decompression day before flights home.
dailyItinerary.why: After the big park days, a slow Puerto Natales day makes the Patagonia plan more humane and bookable.
moments: Walk the waterfront sculptures/views.
Use town services before travel day.
Make dinner the celebration, not another excursion.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Return to Buenos Aires airport buffer
dailyItinerary.overnight: EZE airport hotel / Buenos Aires buffer
dailyItinerary.transport: Fly or transfer back toward Buenos Aires via El Calafate/Puerto Natales routing; keep an overnight buffer before ATL return.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Travel day back north, airport-area hotel, luggage reset, and early night.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If flight schedules require, overnight in Buenos Aires city instead of EZE airport area.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport meals and simple hotel dinner; budget $210.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Protect the international flight with a buffer night; do not same-day connect Patagonia to ATL.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book domestic return with generous padding and confirm baggage allowances.
dailyItinerary.why: The buffer night is what makes this ambitious trip plausible with a baby.
moments: Accept that this is not a sightseeing day.
Choose reliability over romance.
Reset bags and sleep before the long flight home.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Return domestic flight budget is mostly included in Day 1; this covers local transfers and buffer hotel.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

dailyItinerary.title: Fly Buenos Aires to Atlanta
dailyItinerary.transport: Return EZE to ATL on Delta planning snapshot.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Airport morning, stroller gate-check, and flight home.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If flight is late, use hotel late checkout/day room strategy.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport food and baby snacks; budget $110.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Keep the morning simple; infant-in-lap already included in Day 1 flight budget.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm flight times and infant-in-lap documentation requirements.
dailyItinerary.why: A quiet airport day closes a complicated trip without a final logistics scramble.
moments: Use the buffer hotel to make check-in calmer.
Keep snacks/layers accessible.
Plan for a long recovery day at home after arrival.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Local departure costs only; round-trip airfare is allocated on Day 1.
dailyItinerary.pitchTitle: Why this day earns its spot

routeLabel: Buenos Aires → El Calafate → El Chalten → Puerto Natales → Torres del Paine → Buenos Aires

routeMap.note: Real OpenStreetMap route view. Solid blue route lines use cached OSRM driving geometry to follow the roads we would actually drive; dashed clay lines are direct reference legs for non-road or unavailable segments. Numbered day pins may fan out slightly when several days share the same base.
